title: A function can return several separate values
statement: return a, b sends back two separate values, so the caller receives two things rather than one tuple.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: predict the type of a call that returns a comma-separated list
evidence_patterns.signature: predicts two values, or that the second is lost, rather than one tuple

example.item:
def f():
    return 1, 2
x = f()
print(type(x))
example.response: int (or 'error, two values into one variable')

discriminators.vs_slip: Consistent across items and revealed by asking what x holds after x = f(). A slip is a single wrong type.

conflicts_with.label: A function returns one value; several values travel as one tuple

resolved_by.label: A function returns one value; several values travel as one tuple
return hands a value back to the caller and ends the call

sources.citation: Chiodini, L., Moreno Santos, I., Gallidabino, A., Tafliovich, A., Santos, A. L., & Hauswirth, M. (2021). A curated inventory of programming language misconceptions. In Proceedings of the 26th ACM Conference on Innovation and Technology in Computer Science Education (ITiCSE '21), 380-386.
sources.note: Inventory consulted for the misconception name and scope only; progmiscon publishes no licence for its text, so OML's statements and examples are written independently.

provenance.notes: Drafted from the cited literature for the OML seed pack; statement, examples and discriminators are original text. Awaiting maintainer review.
